title: Personal Services Plan — One Plan per Resident and Household Sharing
content:
**Clause.** A resident holds at most 1 Personal Services Plan at a time. Where the tier provides for household sharing, both occupants of a double-occupancy independent living apartment draw from that one plan, and the second occupant never enrolls separately. A new plan may be opened only when the resident has no other plan that is pending start, active, suspended or cancellation pending.

## The clause restated

| Resident's existing personal services plan, as the plan records show it | May a new plan be opened? |
|---|---|
| None on record | Yes |
| A plan pending start | No |
| An active plan | No |
| A suspended plan | No |
| A plan with a cancellation pending | No |
| Only a plan that has ended | Yes |

The test is made on the plan records held for the resident, not on the resident's own account of them.

## Points of judgement

- **Second occupant.** The second occupant of a double-occupancy independent living apartment draws from the plan the household already holds and does not enroll a plan of their own.
- **Ended plans.** A plan that has ended is not pending start, active, suspended or cancellation pending, so it does not stand in the way of a new enrollment.
- **Hypothetical case.** A resident whose only plan is recorded as cancellation pending asks to open a second plan for a different package. The existing plan is in one of the four listed statuses, so no new plan may be opened while it remains so.
